 Recommendation:

 Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A
 RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING THE
 AGNES AVENUE STRIPING DESIGN AND AUTHORIZATION TO PREPARE
 CONSTRUCTION DRAWINGS AND SOLICIT BIDS FOR THE AGNES STRIPING PROJECT,
 FY 2024-2025 (CIP PROJECT NO. 2350|2352.68.145).”

 Background:

 On July 7, 2020, the City Council awarded a construction contract for the Agnes Avenue
 street, water and sewer improvements project (CIP NO. 4011.68.087). The project included
 new striping of Agnes Avenue from Bullis Road to Atlantic Avenue. The striping consists of
 parking brackets on both sides of the street with a center median of approximately thirty (30)
 feet from Thorson Avenue to Atlantic Avenue. On April 5, 2022, the project (CIP NO.
 4011.68.087) was accepted.

 Since the project’s acceptance, there have been comments and concerns about the striping,
 such as vehicles using the center median as a travel lane and trash bins being placed on the

City Council City Council Regular Meeting
  204
  center median. Also, the amount of parking T’s installed is not sufficient for the residents living
 on Agnes Avenue.

 The City of Lynwood is dedicated to maintaining safe and clean streets. Staff sent the request
 to the on-call consultant engineer, Transtech Engineers Inc., to create a new striping design
 on Agnes Avenue from Thorson Avenue to Atlantic Avenue. This project will include additional
 parking spaces and improve safety for drivers. The striping design has been completed and is
 ready to be presented for approval.

 Discussion and Analysis:

 Transtech Engineers Inc., provided several alternatives for striping on Agnes Avenue. After
 reviewing each alternative, staff recommends moving forward with an angled parking striping
 design. The design includes a new slurry seal treatment applied along Agnes Avenue from
 Thorson Avenue to Atlantic Avenue. After the slurry seal treatment, Agnes Avenue, which is
 approximately seventy (70) feet wide, will have twenty (20) feet wide angle parking brackets
 on the north and south sides of the street. Additionally, fourteen (14) feet will be dedicated to
 travel lanes for eastbound and westbound traffic, with a 2-foot centerline marking to clearly
 define the roadway. With this new design, vehicle safety will be increased, and the use of
 existing center median for trash collection will be eliminated. As well, Agnes Avenue from
 Thorson Avenue to Atlantic Avenue will include twenty-five (25) additional parking spaces. The
 total amount of parking spaces will increase from approximately seventy-five (75) parking
 spaces to one hundred (100) parking spaces.

 Staff is recommending that City Council approve the angled parking striping design. Upon
 authorization by the City Council, staff will move forward with creating the construction
 drawings for this project and will proceed with advertising the project for solicitation of bids.

 This Project’s FY 24-25 CIP budget includes $250,000 from Measure M and Measure R.

 Measure R  $125,000
 Total Project Budget  $250,000

 No additional appropriation is needed at this time.

 Recommendation:

 Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A
 RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING A FIFTH
 AMENDMENT TO THE AGREEMENT WITH WATERWORKS TECHNOLOGY, INC. FOR
 THE INTERIM MANAGEMENT OF THE WATER AND SEWER OPERATIONS AND CAPITAL

 AGREEMENTS”.

 Background:

 The City provides water service to approximately 69,900 residents, through about 9,620 water
 services utilizing ninety-five miles of water distribution pipelines and one (1) reservoir and
 booster station. The City’s water supply consists of a mix of local groundwater and imported
 water. The City pumps groundwater from the Central Groundwater Basin, in conjunction with
 the Water Replenishment District of Southern California (WRD) through five (5) active wells
 that are owned and operated by the City. Imported water is sourced from Metropolitan Water
 District (MWD) via Central Basin Municipal Water District (CBMWD).

 The City of Lynwood’s Utilities Division operates and oversees the City’s water and sewer

City Council City Council Regular Meeting
  212
  collection systems including maintaining the water supply, ensuring water quality, maintaining,
 and upgrading the water system and sewer collection system infrastructure and providing
 emergency response. In order to continue to provide utility services to the Lynwood residents,
 the City requires the assistance of a consultant company to provide Utility Support services.
 On June 26, 2024, the City Council approved a fourth amendment to the existing agreement
 with Waterworks Technology, Inc. to extend the contract up to August 31, 2024.

 Discussion and Analysis:

 Waterworks Technology, Inc. has been providing staffing necessary to manage the water and
 sewer systems as well as submit the necessary reports to various State agencies overseeing
 drinking water quality and production. Waterworks Technology, Inc. has also assisted staff
 with the on-going CIP. Currently, Waterworks Technology, Inc. provides the required

at the Cal Cities Annual Conference and Expo. The General Assembly is an important
opportunity where city officials can directly participate in the development of Cal Cities
policy.

Taking place on Oct. 18, the General Assembly is comprised of voting delegates
appointed by each member city; every city has one voting delegate. Your appointed
voting delegate plays an important role during the General Assembly by representing
your city and voting on resolutions.

To cast a vote during the General Assembly, your city must designate a voting
delegate and up to two alternate voting delegates, one of whom may vote if the
designated voting delegate is unable to serve in that capacity. Voting delegates may
either be an elected or appointed official.

Action by Council Required. Consistent with Cal Cities bylaws, a city’s voting delegate
and up to two alternates must be designated by the city council. Please note that
designating the voting delegate and alternates must be done by city council action
and cannot be accomplished by individual action of the mayor or city manager alone.

submission portal by Wed., Sept. 25. When completing the Voting Delegate submission

delegate/alternate records prior to the conference and provide pre-conference
communications with voting delegates.

Conference Registration Required. The voting delegate and alternates must be
registered to attend the conference. They need not register for the entire conference;
they may register for Friday only. Conference registration is open on the Cal Cities

1.  One City One Vote. Each member city has a right to cast one vote on
  matters pertaining to Cal Cities policy.

2.  Designating a City Voting Representative. Prior to the Cal Cities Annual
  Conference and Expo, each city council may designate a voting delegate

  delegate form provided to the Cal Cities Credentials Committee.

  the conference registration area. Voting delegates and alternates must sign
  in at the voting delegate desk. Here they will receive a special sticker on
  their name badge and thus be admitted to the voting area at the General
  Assembly.

4.  Signing Initiated Resolution Petitions. Only those individuals who are voting
  delegates (or alternates), and who have picked up their city’s voting card
  by providing a signature to the credentials committee at the voting
  delegate desk, may sign petitions to initiate a resolution.

  city's voting card and voting tool; and be registered with the credentials
  committee. The voting card may be transferred freely between the voting
  delegate and alternates but may not be transferred to another city official
  who is neither a voting delegate nor alternate.

  be limited to the individual in possession of the voting card and with a
  special sticker on their name badge identifying them as a voting delegate.

  determine the validity of signatures on petitioned resolutions and the right of
  a city official to vote at the General Assembly.

 Recommendation:

 Staff recommends that the City Council conduct the second reading and adoption, read by title
 only, and waive the full reading of Ordinance No. 1782 entitled "AN ORDINANCE OF THE
 CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF
 CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE LYNWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE TO IMPLEMENT
 MINISTERIAL REVIEW OF AFFORDABLE HOUSING PROJECTS ON HOUSING ELEMENT
 SITES TO IMPLEMENT THE LYNWOOD GENERAL PLAN 2021-2029 HOUSING
 ELEMENT".

 Background:

 The City of Lynwood has prepared an update to the city's Housing Element. California's
 Government Code section 65580 mandates each jurisdiction to prepare a Housing Element
 that is incorporated into its General Plan. This is to ensure adequate planning for projected
 housing demand throughout the state. Unlike other elements of the General Plan, the Housing
 Element must be updated by deadlines set forth by the state agency, the Department of
 Housing and Community Development (HCD).

 Discussion and Analysis:

City Council City Council Regular Meeting
  231
  Staff is recommending approval of General Plan Amendment GPA 2024-01 as this will adopt
 the 2021-2029 Housing Element which is necessary for the City to be certified in compliance
 with housing element law. Compliance with housing element law is critical for funding
 eligibility. Several federal, state, and regional funding programs consider housing element
 compliance as an eligibility or ranking criteria.

 The ordinance will make available vacant sites accommodating 151 units and nonvacant
 (underutilized) sites accommodating 516 units toward the lower RHNA. This exceeds the
 minimum 379 units that need to be made available noted in Program 5 of the Housing
 Element. Together with pending projects accommodating 137 units, the City will accommodate
 a total of 804 units on sites suitable for affordable housing following approval of the ordinance,
